engine.formula: y_ ~ treatment + treatment2 + (1 | block) + (1 | unit_id_) +     treatment:treatment2
engine.model: Cox proportional hazards with normal random effects (mixed-effects Cox model)
engine.assumptions: proportional hazards; independent censoring given the random effects; normal random effects

not_used.coxph_frailty: models one random intercept, random terms; the design has block, unit_id_
not_used.coxph: would drop the random terms (block, unit_id_): only with allow_fallback = TRUE

engine.reference: Therneau TM, coxme (R package); Ripatti & Palmgren 2000, Biometrics 56:1016

effect.definition: hazard ratio of a level vs the reference (Cox)

table.statistic_name: robust score chi-squared (Lin-Wei, clustered by unit)

stat_test.reference: Kaplan & Meier 1958 JASA 53:457; Mantel 1966 Cancer Chemother Rep 50:163; Cox 1972 JRSS B 34:187; Grambsch & Therneau 1994 Biometrika 81:515; Royston & Parmar 2013 BMC Med Res Methodol 13:152; Therneau survival (CRAN)
stat_test.note: competing events censored here (cause-specific: Kaplan-Meier is survival net of the competing risk); cumulative incidence in the competing-risks block; median not reached in genotype_2 / primed: report a landmark survival or the RMST; 480 subsamples in 48 units: the robust score test is primary; the plain log-rank, KM and RMST intervals treat subsamples as independent; proportional hazards rejected on the fixed part (cox.zph global p = 0.00199)

table.statistic_name: Gray's test chi-squared (seed rot before germination)

also.reference: Gray 1988 Ann Stat 16:1141; Fine & Gray 1999 JASA 94:496; Putter et al. 2007 Stat Med 26:2389; Gray cmprsk (CRAN)
also.note: 1 - Kaplan-Meier overstates the risk of germination (all at 14: 0.489 vs CIF 0.446)

warnings: competing events (codes 2): the Cox model is cause-specific for event code 1
survival subsamples are not averaged: 48 units kept as clusters of their subsamples (shared frailty)

goal_recovery.test: weighted log-rank fh_0_1 (prespecified), joint over 4 groups
goal_recovery.scale: hazard ratio after t = 5.98811 (piecewise Cox split at change_time; log scale); estimate / true_effect = treatment, all 2 terms in piecewise$terms
goal_recovery.note: hazards not proportional (delayed_effect): one Cox HR (treatment 0.909, treatment2 0.830) averages the phases

groups.note: per treatment cell vs Simitall outcome_model.groups; intervals treat subsamples as independent

recovery.scale: survival fit vs Gaussian (latent) truth: compared by sign and detection; hazard sign reversed
